h1:
Khon Kaen for Nature Lovers
Phu Wiang · Ubol Ratana Dam · Phu Phan Kham
intro: A lot of people treat Khon Kaen as a city you just pass through. But drive about an hour and a bit west of downtown and you hit a different Khon Kaen — forested hills, a big reservoir, and dinosaur fossils that are over a hundred million years old. This plan spreads it over 3 days and 2 nights at an easy pace, nothing crammed, following Phu Wiang, Ubol Ratana Dam, and Phu Phan Kham — with opening hours and entry fees we've already checked.
chips: 🛶 Raft lunch on Ubol Ratana Dam
⛰️ Lake views from Hin Chang Si

blocks.html: Khon Kaen's nature route clusters in the west of the province, around the Ubol Ratana Dam reservoir — a large lake ringed by hills on three sides. To the north sits the Phu Wiang range, where dinosaur fossils were dug up and turned into the province's signature attraction. On the eastern side of the dam is Phu Phan Kham, with a viewpoint looking straight down over the whole reservoir. You can drive between all three in a single day, but if you want to take it easy, spreading it over 3 days works much better.

This trip is best for people with a car (or a rental from downtown), because the main spots sit 50–90 km outside the city and public transport barely reaches them. If you don't have a car you can charter a van or use a daily car-rental service — figure around 1,000–1,400 THB a day for a sedan.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Tracking dinosaurs at Phu Wiang

blocks.html: On day one you drive from downtown Khon Kaen out toward Wiang Kao district, roughly 80–90 km, about an hour and a half. The target is the Phu Wiang Dinosaur Museum and the excavation pits inside the national park. It's a light walking day and easy to do with kids.

items.activity: Leave downtown Khon Kaen, grab breakfast before heading up the hills
items.note: Fill the tank in the city — petrol stations near Wiang Kao are few and far between

items.activity: Phu Wiang Dinosaur Research and Museum Center, Wiang Kao district
items.note: Open Tue–Sun 09:30–16:30, closed Mondays · Thai adults 20 THB, children 10 THB · the skeleton of Phuwiangosaurus sirindhornae is on display

items.activity: Drive up into Phu Wiang National Park to see the dinosaur footprint and bone excavation pits
items.note: Park entry is around 40 THB for Thai adults · several pits are roofed over and only a short walk from the parking area

items.activity: Lunch at a made-to-order shop in Wiang Kao town
items.note: Shops in the district close early — get there before 2 pm or only a few may still be open

items.activity: Tat Fa Waterfall, inside Phu Wiang park (rainy season to early cool season only)
items.note: About a 500 m walk uphill · low water in the dry season, so check the park's page before you go

items.activity: Head back to your lodging on the Ubol Ratana Dam side, or return to the city
items.note: If you've booked a lakeside stay, it's about a 40-minute drive from Wiang Kao to Ubol Ratana

blocks.title: Check before you go
blocks.html: The dinosaur museum is closed every Monday. Tat Fa Waterfall looks best from the rainy season into early cool season (July–December); in the dry months there's almost no water. If you come in the dry season, skip the waterfall and head straight to the dam.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Ubol Ratana Dam and a raft fish lunch

blocks.html: Ubol Ratana Dam was the first multipurpose dam in Isan, about 50 km from downtown Khon Kaen. The spots visitors go for are the dam crest, the riverside park, and the Bang Saen 2 zone, where floating raft restaurants let you eat in the cool breeze. Today is a chill day — no need to rush.

items.activity: Visit the Ubol Ratana Dam crest and photograph the reservoir views
items.note: Morning sun is gentle and the breeze off the water keeps it cool

items.activity: Cycle or stroll the riverside Chaloem Phra Kiat park by the dam
items.note: Some spots rent out bicycles and pedal boats

items.activity: Raft fish lunch in the Bang Saen 2 zone, e.g. Krua Khru Or
items.note: Signature dishes are grilled fish, fried sheatfish, and tom yum · fish prices vary by size, so ask the per-kilo price before ordering to avoid surprises

items.activity: Relax on the raft and let kids paddle in the shallows beside it
items.note: Put life jackets on small kids — the reservoir water is deep

items.activity: Stop at a lakeside café, or Khiri Thara, for sunset views
items.note: The evening light is lovely and good for photos

items.activity: Return to your lodging, or head into Khon Kaen for dinner
items.note: If you're staying by the dam tonight, the night air is cooler than in the city

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: The raft restaurants by the dam are decent overall, with the atmosphere being the real draw. But many of them price fish by weight without clear signage, and some reviews complain that prices don't match the menu. Ask for the per-kilo price and confirm it before they start cooking, so you're not caught off guard when the bill comes.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Hin Chang Si and the Phu Phan Kham view

blocks.html: On the last day you head up to the Phu Phan Kham side. The highlight is Hin Chang Si, a wide rock terrace on the ridge looking down over the entire Ubol Ratana Dam reservoir, with the Phu Wiang and Phu Kao ranges off in the distance. It's a viewpoint that hasn't been overrun yet — quieter than the dam, a calm way to end the trip.

items.activity: Set off for the Hin Chang Si viewpoint
items.note: Open daily 08:00–17:00 · park entry Thai adults 20 THB, children 10 THB

items.activity: Walk the Hin Chang Si rock terrace, taking in the reservoir views and oddly shaped rock formations
items.note: Morning brings thin mist and gentle sun — the easiest time to walk

items.activity: Photograph the rock formations and panoramic angles
items.note: Parts of the rock terrace get slippery with morning dew — wear rubber-soled shoes with grip

items.activity: Head down and have lunch at an Isan restaurant on the way back
items.note: Som tam, grilled chicken, and laab are easy to find along the route

items.activity: Stop for souvenirs before reaching the city
items.note: Mu yo, Isan sausage, and Chinese sausage are popular Khon Kaen souvenirs

items.activity: Back in downtown Khon Kaen — trip done
items.note: Leave buffer time for an evening flight or bus

blocks.text: What each of these nature spots is actually like

items.name: Phu Wiang National Park
items.blurb: The first place dinosaurs were excavated in Thailand, with dig pits, footprints, bones, and Tat Fa Waterfall in the forest. Easy walking and good for families.

items.name: Ubol Ratana Dam
items.blurb: A big lake with floating raft restaurants, lakeside cycling, and fish lunches in the breeze. Great for a rest day without much walking.

items.name: Hin Chang Si, Phu Phan Kham
items.blurb: A rock terrace on the ridge looking down over the whole reservoir. Still not crowded, quiet, and lovely at sunrise and sunset.

blocks.text: Rough budget per person (3 days, 2 nights)

items: Museum + 3 park entry fees — around 80–120 THB total (Thai rate)
Car rental + fuel — about 1,000–1,400 THB/day, split among the group; with 4 people that's roughly 700–1,000 THB each for the whole trip
Lakeside / in-town lodging — lakeside resorts start at 700–1,500 THB/night · in-town hotels come in many tiers
Food — 80–200 THB per meal · a group raft fish lunch runs around 300–500 THB/person
Estimated total — roughly 2,500–4,000 THB/person, depending on lodging level and how many people split the car

blocks.text: When's the best time to do this route

blocks.html: The best window is November to February — cool weather, plenty of water in the reservoir, clear views from Hin Chang Si, and comfortable raft time without the heat. Next best is the start of the rainy season (July–September), when Tat Fa Waterfall is full and the forest is green, though parts of the climb get slippery. From March to May it's very hot and the waterfall dries up; if you come then, lean on the dam and the air-conditioned museum instead.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Always check the Facebook pages for Phu Wiang and Phu Kao–Phu Phan Kham parks before you head out, because in parts of the rainy season they temporarily close the waterfall trails or viewpoints, and opening hours can shift with the season.

faq.q: Can you do Phu Wiang, Ubol Ratana Dam, and Phu Phan Kham in one day?
faq.a: Yes, if you start early and have your own car, but it'll be tiring and very rushed, since the three spots are 40–90 km apart. Spreading it over 2–3 days is far more relaxed, especially if you're traveling with kids or older family members.

faq.q: When is the Phu Wiang Dinosaur Museum open and how much is entry?
faq.a: It's open Tuesday to Sunday, 09:30–16:30, closed Mondays. Entry is 20 THB for Thai adults and 10 THB for children; foreign adults 60 THB, children 30 THB. Double-check the museum's page, as hours may shift on public holidays.

faq.q: Where is Hin Chang Si and is it hard to get up there?
faq.a: Hin Chang Si is a rock terrace on the ridge on the Phu Phan Kham side, looking down over the Ubol Ratana Dam reservoir. You can drive almost all the way to the viewpoint and walk a little farther. It's open daily 08:00–17:00, park entry 20 THB for Thai adults and 10 THB for children.

faq.q: Can you do this route without your own car?
faq.a: Doing it yourself by public transport is very hard, since the main spots are outside the city and buses don't reach them. The convenient options are renting a car to drive yourself from downtown Khon Kaen, or chartering a van with a driver by the day.

faq.q: Roughly how much is a raft fish lunch at Ubol Ratana Dam?
faq.a: Food is priced by the menu, and grilled or fried fish is charged by weight. Overall a group meal runs around 300–500 THB per person. Ask the per-kilo price and confirm before ordering, since some shops post only the price of their cheapest fish.
